configurePresets.name: conf-crossfire-host-debug
configurePresets.description: The pico_hostmode build, and the only configuration that registers this project's tests. binaryDir is overridden because conf-crossfire-base points at ${sourceDir}/build, which the rp2040 and rp2350 firmware presets also use -- so configuring this one clobbered whichever firmware tree was there, and pointing the test runner at it found firmware and no tests. build-host is the directory that was already being configured by hand for exactly this reason.

configurePresets.name: conf-crossfire-pico2-debug
configurePresets.description: The rp2350 (Pico 2) firmware build. binaryDir is overridden so the RP2350 presets keep a tree of their own instead of sharing ${sourceDir}/build with the rp2040 ones: two different chips in one directory means switching boards always reconfigures from an incompatible cache, and light-configure.ps1's guard turns that into a -Force every time rather than letting both builds simply coexist. See conf-crossfire-link-debug for the command-line-length problem a longer tree name can cause on an RP2 tree -- 'build-pico2' was configured and built to confirm it stays under that limit.

configurePresets.name: conf-crossfire-link-debug
configurePresets.description: The 2-board SPI-linked transport test rig: one local USB-MIDI device plus a virtual device reached over a pair of one-way SPI links to an identically-built peer, standing in for the custom PCB's other ports. Exists as a preset because CROSSFIRE_ENABLE_SPI_LINK defaults OFF, so crossfire_spi_link.c was compiled by nothing a fresh checkout could run -- CI included. The display is off because the link consumes both hardware SPI peripherals. NOTE it shares ${sourceDir}/build with the other firmware presets rather than taking a tree of its own, and that is not laziness: a longer binaryDir name overflows the Windows 32KB command-line limit during configure, because CMake invokes `ninja -t restat` with every generated cmake_install.cmake path listed and the pico-sdk tree produces hundreds. build-link failed on exactly that while an identical configure into a two-character directory succeeded; CMAKE_SKIP_INSTALL_RULES does not avoid it. light-configure.ps1's collision guard already covers sharing a tree, and CI gets a fresh runner per matrix leg.

configurePresets.name: conf-crossfire-mini-stm32h7-debug
configurePresets.description: WeAct MiniSTM32H7xx (STM32H743VIT6) on bare CMSIS, headless. Inherits conf-light-base rather than conf-crossfire-base: that base carries conf-light-pico-base, which sets LIGHT_SYSTEM=PICO_SDK and a PICO_SDK_PATH, neither of which means anything here. The status display is off because it is a Pico-OLED-1.3 expansion board that plugs into a Pico header and does not exist on this target -- USB-MIDI forwarding and console output are what this build is for. TinyUSB is compiled from a checkout resolved by light_usb rather than supplied by an SDK; see that project's CMakeLists.

configurePresets.name: conf-crossfire-link-pico2-debug
configurePresets.description: The SPI-link rig on an RP2350 Pico 2 rather than an rp2040. Same link pins -- GP17/18/19 carry SPI0 on both parts. Shares ${sourceDir}/build-pico2 with conf-crossfire-pico2-debug, which is the same arrangement the rp2040 presets have in ${sourceDir}/build: the split is by CHIP, so an rp2040 tree and an rp2350 tree can both exist, while the two configurations of one chip still take turns under light-configure.ps1's collision guard.

configurePresets.name: conf-crossfire-link-stm32h7-debug
configurePresets.description: The H743 with the SPI link enabled, for testing the link against a Pico peer. Shares build-mini-stm32h7 with the plain H7 preset -- light-configure.ps1's guard covers the collision, and a CMSIS tree is small enough that its directory name does not approach the Windows command-line limit the RP2 trees run into. Headless like the plain H7 build: the display is a Pico expansion board.

configurePresets.name: conf-crossfire-trace
configurePresets.description: As conf-crossfire-debug but at TRACE verbosity. conf-light-pico is inherited because it supplies LIGHT_PLATFORM and LIGHT_BOARD, without which light_platform.cmake has no board to select a chip and toolchain from. Omitting it meant this preset could only configure by inheriting a board from whatever cache already occupied build/, so it appeared to work in a used tree and failed in a fresh one. CROSSFIRE_ENABLE_SPI_LINK is deliberately left at its default: that option builds the two-board SPI-linked test rig, which is not what a trace build of the ordinary firmware should be.

configurePresets.name: conf-crossfire-release
configurePresets.description: As conf-crossfire-debug but built for release. See conf-crossfire-trace for why conf-light-pico is inherited and why this has its own binaryDir.
